name: Trend
summary: Numeric delta indicator. A small chip showing change vs a baseline: '+12.4%', '−3 units', '+$420'. Auto-derives tone from the sign (positive=accent, negative=danger, zero=neutral) unless the consumer flips polarity (some KPIs are 'lower is better' — e.g. churn, page load time). Used inside KPI cards, Stat blocks, table rows, and AI summaries.

delta.description: Signed delta. Positive renders an UpArrow + accent; negative renders a DownArrow + danger; zero renders a tilde + neutral.

polarity.description: positive-is-good: default. negative-is-good: flips tone (lower = good — churn, time-to-resolve, latency). neutral: no tone — just direction.

compact.description: Drops the unit suffix and renders just '↑ 12.4' (when paired with a parent label that names the unit).

rules: aria-label spells out the delta: 'Up 12.4 percent versus previous period' (the consumer passes the period text).
Color is never the only cue — pair with an UpArrow / DownArrow glyph.
Digits render in tabular-nums (.lumen-tnum) so trends in a column align vertically.

do: Use Trend inside KPI cards next to the headline metric.
Use polarity='negative-is-good' for churn, latency, time-to-resolve.
Always pair with the period in nearby text ('vs last week').
Use compact=true inside tight table cells where the unit is implied.
dont: Don't paint positive deltas in danger red, or negative in lime green, by overriding tones. Use the polarity prop.
Don't render Trend without a baseline reference somewhere ('vs last 7 days').

changelog.note: Initial Trend contract. Polarity-aware tone, tabular-nums alignment, compact mode for tables.
